children.translated_text: <s>Pratyakṣa-pariccheda</s> (Chapter on Perception)
Having bowed to the teacher, the Lord of the World, for the sake of children of little intellect,

children.text: Chogs. kyi. grags. pa'i. lugs. mñan. phyir

children.translated_text: the <s>Tarkabhāṣā</s> is set forth.
in order to hear the doctrine of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>,
as the cause of accomplishing all human aims; therefore <s>pramāṇa</s> is elucidated first.
Here indeed, persons who act with deliberation, desiring [their goals], pursue the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition)
that is <s>pramāṇa</s>. That itself is correct cognition, because it is free from the defects of doubt and error.

children.text: अविसंवादकं ज्ञानं लोके सम्यग्ज्ञानमभिधीयते । न च
children.translated_text: Non-discordant cognition is called correct cognition in the world. And there is no non-discordance
in the case of doubtful or erroneous cognition. Just as, for example, the cognition 'Is it a post or a person?'

children.text: पुरुषो वेतिज्ञानस्य, मरीचिकासु वा जलज्ञानस्य । अपूर्वो गोचरो
children.translated_text: or the cognition of water in a mirage. 'Previously unapprehended' is the object
of this — hence 'having a previously unapprehended object.' The object is the referent, such as a pot. Therefore, cognition that arises from that
and is capable of leading to that object is <s>pramāṇa</s>.
<s>Pramāṇa</s> is correct cognition of a previously unapprehended object. 'That by which an object is cognized'—

children.text: ननु ज्ञानं कर्तृ पुरुषं प्रयोज्यमर्थं कर्मभूतं यदि कदा
चिन्न प्रापयति तत्कथमप्रापकत्वात् प्रमाणं स्यात् ? उच्यते ।
children.translated_text: then how can it be <s>pramāṇa</s>, since it fails to lead? Reply:

children.text: न हि ज्ञानेन पुरुषो गले पादुकान्यायेन बलादर्थे प्रवर्तयि
children.translated_text: It is not the case that cognition must forcibly engage the person in the object, as in the maxim of 'shoes around the neck.' Rather,
a certainty of this form should be generated: 'This is the true nature of the thing, not otherwise.' If

children.text: निश्चयो जनयितव्यः । स चेत्तेन कृतः, एतावतैवास्य प्रामाण्य
children.translated_text: that [certainty] has been produced by it, then to that extent alone its validity

children.text: मविरुद्धम् । पुरुषस्तु तत्र प्रयोजनवशात् प्रवर्ततामृते प्रयोजनं
children.translated_text: is uncontradicted. As for the person, let him engage on account of purpose,

children.text: न प्रवर्तताम्, अर्थो वा योगिपिशाचादिभिरपह्रियताम् । ज्ञानस्य
children.translated_text: or let him not engage in the absence of purpose; or let the object be carried away by <s>yogins</s>, <s>piśācas</s> (demons), and the like.
What loss is there to the cognition?
Objection: If cognition, which is the agent, sometimes does not lead the person, who is to be impelled, to the object, which is the karmic object,

children.text: कत्वं च दृष्टार्थप्रापणात् । न च यद्दृष्टं तत्प्राप्यते, क्षणिकत्वात्
children.translated_text: consists in leading to the apprehended object. But what is seen is not [the same as what is] obtained, due to momentariness.

children.text: किंच रूपं दृष्टं, प्राप्यते च स्प्रष्टव्यम् । ततोऽन्यद्दृष्टमन्यत्
children.translated_text: Moreover, form is seen, but what is obtained is a tangible. Therefore, since something different is seen and something different

children.text: प्राप्यत इत्यप्रतीतप्रापणात् कथं प्रामाण्यमस्य संगच्छताम् । न ।
children.translated_text: is obtained, how can its validity be established, since it leads to what is not apprehended? No [this is not a valid objection].

children.text: यदि नाम वस्तुतोऽन्यदेव प्राप्यते तथापि दृष्टमेव मया प्राप्त
children.translated_text: Even if in reality something different is obtained, nevertheless, because of the determination of identity—'What I saw is what I
obtained'—it is said to lead to what is apprehended. As for the cognition of water in a mirage
and the like, since it is incapable of leading [to the object], it is simply not a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Objection: The validity of cognition consists in non-discordance, and non-discordance
'this is capable of leading, this is not.' And by the mere arising of cognition, the distinction between erroneous and non-erroneous

children.text: वधार्यते । ततश्च कथं तत्सम्यग्ज्ञानमिति चेत् । नैष दोषः ।
children.translated_text: is not determined. How then can that be correct cognition? This is no fault.
Although from the mere arising of cognition as such, the distinction between the two cannot be determined,
nevertheless, from the arising of a specific cognition, the distinction of one is stated as follows:
For if a person of dull intellect is unable to determine the non-discordance of cognition
merely from its arising, still, by observing purposive actions such as burning, cooking, bathing, immersion, drinking,
and surfacing from afar, or by observing rising smoke and the like,
he determines it. But a person of keen intellect determines it by a more vivid <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) itself,
not through the attainment of purposive action. If validity is characterized by non-discordance,
then
how can the validity of auditory cognition be established, since it does not lead to the apprehended object?
No [this objection does not hold].
For validity is the apprehension of the true nature of the object. And that is possible
even without the attainment of external purposive action. As has been stated:
cognition; purposive efficacy is its foundation.' Non-discordance [is explained thus].
'<s>Pramāṇa</s> is non-discordant
Since the word (<s>śabda</s>) fulfills its purpose
by mere hearing alone, hearing itself is the purposive efficacy in that case. Just as
the mere seeing of the sun, moon, clouds, pictures, and the like constitutes their purposive efficacy. As stated:
'The cognition of the true nature of the knowable is accepted; therein lies the efficacy of action.'
But first,
a deliberate person, desiring purposive action, engages with water, fire, and such things precisely because of doubt

children.text: र्तते । यदि नाम तस्यैव नास्ति सन्देहो मे वर्तत इति
children.translated_text: about purposive efficacy. Even if he himself has no doubt [about it],
still, in the absence of validating or invalidating <s>pramāṇas</s>, a reasonable doubt arising
is prevented by what? Therefore it is established that — from the practice of uninterrupted purposive activity that has been achieved,
a person engages in objects through the arising of vivid perception alone; while a person of dull intellect [engages]

children.text: ताद्रूप्यानुमानादिति । अत एव तु प्रत्यक्षस्य स्वतः प्रामाण्यम् ।
children.translated_text: through inference of similarity. And hence, perception has intrinsic validity;

children.text: कस्यचित्तु परतः । योगिज्ञानस्य स्वसंवेदनस्य च स्वत एव
children.translated_text: for some, however, [validity is] extrinsic. The <s>yogin's</s> cognition and self-awareness have intrinsic

children.text: प्रामाण्यम् । अनुमानस्य तु निश्चयात्मकत्वात् स्वत एव प्रामा
children.translated_text: validity alone. And inference, being of the nature of certainty, also has intrinsic

children.text: ण्यम् । तेनायमर्थः--प्रथमत एव यद्विज्ञानं विषये प्रवृत्तं तदेव
children.translated_text: validity. Thus the meaning is this: whatever cognition first arises regarding an object, that alone

children.text: प्रमाणम् । न तु तत्रैव पश्चाद्भावि ज्ञानान्तरमपि । गृहीतग्राहि
children.translated_text: is <s>pramāṇa</s>; but a subsequent cognition regarding the very same object is not. Because it apprehends what has already been apprehended,

children.text: त्वेन तस्याप्रामाण्यात् । यथा घटं निर्विकल्पकेन ज्ञानेन दृष्ट्वा
children.translated_text: it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Just as, after seeing a pot through <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) cognition,
subsequently regarding that very same object, the <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual) cognition 'This is a pot'

children.text: स्मरणरूपम् । यथा वा पर्वतादौ धूमं दृष्ट्वा वह्निर
children.translated_text: is of the nature of memory. Or just as, after seeing smoke on a mountain and the like, the inferential cognition 'There is fire here,'
and then once again the inferential cognition 'There is fire here' regarding the same [object].
When it is said that correct cognition is <s>pramāṇa</s>, by implication, the validity of the sense faculties and the like, which are inert by nature,
is negated, since they lack the capacity for discernment. For the capacity for discernment
is the capacity to know. And that is the very own nature of cognition alone. How then can it be
the nature of the sense faculties and the like, which are non-cognitive?
Objection: Without actually reaching the object through purposive action, it cannot be ascertained
That [<s>pramāṇa</s>] is of two kinds: <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference).
<s>Pratyakṣa</s> is that which has 'reached' (pratigata) the sense faculty (<s>akṣa</s>).
The sense faculty (<s>akṣa</s>) is the <s>indriya</s> (sense organ), designated as eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body. Cognition that arises from it
is called <s>pratyakṣa</s>
(perception). Objection: If cognition dependent on a sense organ is <s>pratyakṣa</s>,
then the three kinds of cognition to be discussed — mental and others — since they do not arise from a sense organ, would not be <s>pratyakṣa</s>.
To this it is replied: The statement 'that which has reached the sense faculty' was presented merely
to indicate the etymology of the word <s>pratyakṣa</s>. The ground for the application
of the word <s>pratyakṣa</s> should be understood, by conventional usage, as the direct apprehension of the object,
like the word <s>paṅkaja</s> (lotus, lit. 'born in mud'). Therefore, self-awareness and other cognitions too, since they directly apprehend the object that is self-awareness in nature,
are established as expressible by the word <s>pratyakṣa</s>.
is <s>anumāna</s> (inference). After the apprehension of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the recollection of the relation between the mark and what it marks,
the cognition that arises regarding a property-bearer such as a mountain, having as its object a thing that is hidden from perception — that alone is denoted
by the word <s>anumāna</s>. And this too should be understood by conventional usage.
'That by which an object is measured is <s>māna</s> (measure).' The prefix 'anu' means 'after.' A measure that comes after

children.text: द्विविधवचनेन एकं त्रीणि चत्वारि पञ्च षडिति विप्रति

children.translated_text: are rejected. Thus: 'Perception alone is the single <s>pramāṇa</s>' — so says
the <s>Cārvāka</s>
'Perception, inference, and verbal testimony' — so says
the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>
. 'Perception, inference, analogy, and verbal testimony' — so says
the <s>Naiyāyika</s>
. 'Perception, inference, verbal testimony, analogy, and presumption' — so says
the <s>Prābhākara</s>
. 'Perception, inference, verbal testimony, analogy, presumption, and non-apprehension' — so says
the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>.
By the statement 'two kinds,' the conflicting views [that there is] one, three, four, five, or six

children.text: पुनर्यदुक्तं तदन्यथाद्वित्वनिरासार्थम् । तथा हि वैयाकरणो ब्रूते
children.translated_text: is for the purpose of rejecting any other [understanding of] twoness. Thus the grammarian says:
'The two <s>pramāṇas</s> are perception and verbal testimony.'

children.text: Here is quoted the following Sloka-

children.translated_text: By the statement 'two kinds,' when twoness is established, what is further stated — 'perception and inference' —

children.text: णेति प्रतिपाद्यते । तथाहि--स खलु प्रत्यक्षलक्षणं परप्रति
children.translated_text: of inference. For he formulates a definition of perception for the purpose of communicating it to others.

children.text: पादनाय प्रणयति । परस्य च बुद्धिर्न प्रत्यक्षा । किं तर्हि
children.translated_text: And the mind of another is not directly perceptible. Rather,
it is to be inferred from effects such as bodily and verbal behavior. Therefore, inference based on effect as mark
is necessarily
accepted by him. And for the purpose of denying the other world, he employs
a proof called non-apprehension. Thus he himself operates with inference as a <s>pramāṇa</s>,
and yet says 'inference is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>' —
how can the <s>Cārvāka</s> not be considered mad
Here it is demonstrated that the <s>Cārvāka</s> must necessarily accept the validity
And non-discordance does not obtain without a relation.
And there is no

children.text: शब्दानां बाह्यार्थेन सह कश्चित्सम्बन्धोऽस्ति । तथा हि—
children.translated_text: relation whatsoever between words and external objects. For —

children.text: शब्दार्थयोः सम्बन्धो भवन् तादात्म्यं तदुत्पत्तिर्वा भवेत् ।
children.translated_text: If there were a relation between word and meaning, it would be either identity or causal origination.

children.text: तत्र न तावत्तादात्म्यं शब्दार्थयोः, अत्यन्तभेदेन प्रतिभासनात् ।
children.translated_text: Now, there is no identity between word and meaning, since they appear as completely distinct.
For identity means oneness. If oneness is accepted even for things that appear differently,
then the absurd consequence of oneness between cows and horses and the like would follow. Nor is there causal origination [of meaning from word],
due to the absence of positive and negative concomitance. Therefore it cannot be said that there is causal origination.
For a pot and similar objects are seen to arise from their own causes — a lump of clay,
a stick, water, a potter's wheel, and the like — without any operation of words.

children.text: दृश्यते । शब्दोऽपि बाह्यार्थं विनैव पुरुषेच्छामात्रेण ताल्वा
children.translated_text: A word too arises merely from human volition, from the operation of the palate and other [articulatory organs], without any external object.
Now, if there is some real relation between word and meaning characterized by the 'expressible-expressor' relationship,
different from both identity and causal origination,
then:
In that case, even a person who does not know the convention should have a definite cognition of the meaning
from a word when it is uttered, by the mere capacity [of the word],

children.text: प्रतीतिः प्राप्ता, योग्यतामात्रेणैव प्रदीपात् घटादिप्रतीतिवत् । न
children.translated_text: just as there is cognition of a pot from a lamp. But this is not the case. For
a fresh person who has just arrived from the Coconut Island (<s>Nālikeradvīpa</s>),
even upon hearing the word 'agni,' does not cognize any meaning from the word 'agni.' Now, if it is said
that a word becomes capable of conveying this or that meaning only in dependence on this or that convention —

children.text: इत्युच्यते । तन्न । न ह्येवमस्य प्रामाण्यमवतिष्टते । सर्वत्र
children.translated_text: that is not so. For its validity does not hold in this way, since convention is possible everywhere.

children.text: सङ्केतस्य योग्यत्वात् । ततो न ज्ञायते किं विवक्षितार्थमाह,
children.translated_text: Therefore one cannot know whether the speaker states the intended meaning

children.text: आहो स्विदन्यं वेति । अस्तु वा अन्य एव कश्चित्सम्बन्धः ।
children.translated_text: or something else. Or let there be some other relation entirely.

children.text: तथा च सोऽपि केन सम्बन्धेन तयोः सम्बद्ध इति प्रष्टव्यः ।
children.translated_text: Even so, by what relation is that [relation] related to the two [word and meaning]? — this must be asked.

children.text: अन्येन चतुर्थेन सम्बन्धेनेति चेत्, चतुर्थोऽपि तेषु केन
children.translated_text: If by a fourth relation, then by what relation is that fourth related to them?

children.text: सम्बन्धेन सम्बद्धः ? पञ्चमेन केनचिच्चेत्, सोऽपि केने
children.translated_text: If by some fifth, then by what is that related?
— in this infinite regress, if the last is not established, the earlier ones are not established either. Now, if [it is said that]

children.text: एव शब्दार्थयोः सम्बन्ध इति चेत् । तन्न । यो न सम्बद्धः
children.translated_text: the relation between word and meaning is itself unrelated [to them] — that is not so. How can something that is not related

children.text: स कथं सम्बन्धो भवति घटस्येव पटः । अथ वक्तव्यं सम्ब
children.translated_text: be a relation? — like a cloth to a pot. Now, if one were to say that the very nature of the relation

because even smokeless
fire

'Doubt arises only when it depends on the recollection of a specific difference;

by that common property, <s>prameyatva</s> (cognizability), smoke-hood, effecthood, and the like are,

inference of

In response: Is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) that qualified cognition necessarily involves the grasping of a separate qualifier,
or that it necessarily involves the experience of a qualifier of any kind? In the first alternative, there is refutation by direct perception,

Thus

Thus, since the universal as postulated by the opponents cannot withstand critical examination,
the mere entity — distinguished from what is not of that nature — alone
is the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), denoted by the word <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), serving as the basis for conventional usage, and is faultless as determined — this is established.

That which, being qualified for apprehension, is not apprehended in a given locus, is the object of the convention of non-existence there,

"With regard to what was previously

they say. Others, however, hold that real consciousness is free from the stain of all representations,
like a pure crystal. These representations are entirely false,

children.text: एवाविद्यया दर्शिताः प्रकाशन्ते । तस्मात् ग्राह्यं नाम नास्त्येव ।
children.translated_text: manifested by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and appear as such. Therefore, the apprehended simply does not exist.
Since the apprehended does not exist,
the apprehender-nature of consciousness, which is relative to it,

children.text: नास्तीति । माध्यमिकानां तु दर्शने तदपि विज्ञानं न परमा
children.translated_text: also does not exist. But in the view of the <s>Mādhyamika</s>s, even that consciousness is not ultimately

children.text: र्थसत्, विचारासहत्वात् । स्वभावेन हि युक्तं पारमार्थिक
children.translated_text: real, because it cannot withstand analysis. For what possesses an intrinsic nature is called ultimately real

children.text: मुच्यते लोके । न चास्य विचारतः कश्चित्स्वभावो घटते
children.translated_text: in the world. But no intrinsic nature of it is tenable under analysis —
whether one or many, because it cannot withstand the analysis stated earlier. As it is said —
Even consciousness is not accepted by the wise as ultimately real,
because it is devoid of the nature of being one or many, like a sky-lotus.
Thus. And <s>Kīrtipāda</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] has also said —

children.text: भावा येन निरूप्यन्ते तद्रूपं नास्ति तत्त्वतः ।
children.translated_text: The form by which entities are analyzed does not exist in reality,

children.text: यस्मादेकमनेकं वा रूपं तेषु न विद्यते ॥
children.translated_text: since neither a unitary nor a plural form is found in them.
Thus. And the <s>Alaṅkārakāra</s> [<s>Dharmottara</s>] has also said —

children.text: यदा तु न विकल्पस्य न चान्यस्य प्रमाणता ।
children.translated_text: When neither conceptual thought nor anything else has the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge),
then even if everything is disintegrating, who is to blame?
Even the distinction of bound and liberated does not exist in the ultimate sense;
for those who see equally everywhere, distinction simply does not appear.

children.text: इति ॥ प्रयोगः पुनरेवम्--यदेकानेकस्वभावं न भवति न
children.translated_text: Thus. The formal argument is as follows: what does not have the nature of being one or many

children.text: तत्परमार्थसत्, यथा व्योमकमलम्, एकानेकस्वभावं च न
children.translated_text: is not ultimately real, like a sky-lotus. And consciousness does not have the nature of being one or many —
this is the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). This reason is not unestablished,

children.text: हेतुः । साकारे ज्ञाने बहिरर्थ इव एकानेकस्वभावायोग्यत्वस्य
children.translated_text: since for <s>sākāra</s> (representational) cognition, the impossibility of being one or many is clearly evident, just as for external objects.
For what the world regards as the domain of external objects is, for the proponent of representations,

children.text: साकारवादिनो ज्ञानम् । ततो यत्तस्य बहिर्भावे बाधकं तदे
children.translated_text: nothing but cognition. Therefore, what refutes the external existence of that

children.text: वान्तर्भावेऽपि बाधकम् । न हि स्थूलमेकमनेकं च परमाणु
children.translated_text: also refutes its internal existence. For the gross, whether one or many, is not accepted even in atomic
form.
If the form of what is of the nature of consciousness is one and gross,

children.text: यदि वाऽनेकः परमाणुशो भिन्नः उभयथाऽपि बाह्यार्थपक्ष
children.translated_text: or if it is many, differentiated atom by atom — in either case, the refutation that pertains to the external-object thesis
cannot be removed. For that refutation does not depend on the externality of the cognition,

children.text: दूषणम्! येन तद्भावेन भवेत् । मूर्तिनिमित्तं बाधकम्;
children.translated_text: such that it would apply only in that mode. The refutation is based on materiality;

children.text: नामूर्ते विज्ञानात्मनि इत्यपि निस्सारम् । साकारतायां विज्ञान
children.translated_text: and the claim that it does not apply to the immaterial nature of consciousness is also without substance, because cognition too is material if it has representations.
For this very
form that extends across
spatial locations
is what is called materiality.
Alternatively, this is the analysis: what appears — it cannot be one,
In the <s>Tarkabhāṣā</s> composed by the great <s>paṇḍita</s> monk <s>Mokṣākaragupta</s>
of the glorious great <s>Jagaddala</s> monastery, the chapter on inference for others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) is completed.
has been produced by me,
Having composed this <s>Tarkabhāṣā</s>, whatever merit
by that merit may this world attain Buddhahood.
The <s>Tarkabhāṣā</s> is completed.
